what: Sandisk makes NAND flash memory, the chips used in solid-state drives, memory cards and phones. It was spun out of Western Digital in 2025 and runs manufacturing jointly with Kioxia in Japan.
customers: Cloud and enterprise data centre operators, phone and PC makers, and retail buyers of memory cards and drives.
money: NAND chips, enterprise and client SSDs, memory cards
moat: Flash fabs cost tens of billions to build, and its long-running joint venture with Kioxia shares that cost across two companies.
risks: Memory is the most cyclical part of the chip industry: prices and profits swing violently
It depends on a joint venture it does not fully control
A single downturn can erase several years of profit
It is a young standalone company without a long track record
opportunities: AI storage demand has pushed flash prices sharply higher, lifting revenue about 175% in the last year
High-capacity enterprise SSDs are a faster-growing, better-priced segment
Low debt means it can withstand a downcycle better than in the past
watch: NAND contract prices and whether supply discipline among the handful of producers holds.
